text: The elder, to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.
Beloved, I pray that in every way you may prosper and be in good health, just as your soul prospers.
It gave me great joy when brothers came and testified about your truthfulness—how you walk in the truth.

versions.text: It gave me great joy when brothers came and testified to your truth—how you walk in the truth.
versions.explanation: "Testified to your truth" is awkward in English and unclear when read aloud; σου τῇ ἀληθείᾳ refers to Gaius's faithfulness/truthfulness, so "testified about your truthfulness" is both clearer and closer to the sense.

text: I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
Beloved, you are acting faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, and strangers at that.
They have testified to your love before the church. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God,
for they set out for the sake of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.
So we ought to support such people, that we may be fellow workers with the truth.
I wrote something to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, will not welcome us.

So if I come, I will bring up what he is doing: spreading malicious nonsense about us. And not content with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers himself, and he stops those who want to welcome them, and throws them out of the church.

versions.text: So if I come, I will bring up what he is doing: spreading malicious nonsense about us. And not content with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers himself, and he stops those who want to and throws them out of the church.
versions.explanation: "Those who want to" leaves the verb dangling, which is confusing for oral reading; supplying "welcome them" makes the implied object of βουλομένους explicit and lets the sentence land cleanly.

text: Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God.
Demetrius is well spoken of by everyone—and by the truth itself. We add our testimony as well, and you know that our testimony is true.
I had much to write to you, but I would rather not write with pen and ink.
I hope to see you soon, and we will talk face to face.
Peace to you. The friends here greet you. Greet the friends there, each by name.
